headline: Proposed revisions to the school fundraising policy and approval of two more parent groups' use of the district name.
summary: Committee members will consider revisions to Students 536, Fundraising Activities, and a request to let two more parent groups use the district's name, logo, and likeness. They will also receive the Employee Handbook for information only.
items: Parent group approval for use of district name, logo, and likeness under CAF 215

Students 536: Fundraising Activities FUND RAISING ACTIVITIES    
Purpose: 
The Board recognizes that students, employees, approved parent/ teacher organizations, 
approved athletic groups, staff and others may wish to engage in fundraising activities to support 
the programs, or offerings provided by the Manchester School District.  
Since the general public may see such fundraising efforts as carrying the endorsement of the 
Manchester School District, all such fundraising activities require the prior approval of the 
Superintendent and/or his/her designee. All fundraising activities must have a clear purpose/goal. 
Fundraising activities governed explicitly by the policy include, but are not limited to:,  
 GoFundMe, Donors Choose or other similar web pagesonline platforms., 
 C cookie dough, candles, books, restaurant/vendor discount cards and other merchandise. 
 Calendar and Rraffles Fundraiser (requires city permit). 
 , Aauctions, restaurant/vendor discount cards, book sales,. 
 SSponsorships.,  
 Walk or read-a-thons, or similar activities.  
 Aany other type of solicitation conducted on behalf of a District school, team program, 
club or organization.  
 Crowd-funding by employees on behalf of the District is governed by Fiscal 909 and 
should not include items supplied by the general fund unless funds have been exhausted.   
This policy shall not apply to bake sales where the anticipated revenue will not exceed five 
hundred dollars ($500.00) in compliance Safety and Transportation -1022 Wellness and 
Nutrition Policy. .Crowd-funding by employees on behalf of the District is governed by Fiscal 
909.  
 
The Superintendent or designee shall have the authority to impose conditions, limitations or 
restrictions on any district associated fundraising activities in addition to the requirements of this 
policy as is deemed warranted or as dictated by accepted accounting standards and practices.  
I. General Fundraising Guidelines: The following conditions shall apply to all fundraising 
activities:  
 
A. All fundraising that is intended to benefit the Manchester School District, its schools, 
students, academic or athletic programs shall require the following:  
 
1. A written agreement approved by the building principal and the Superintendent or 
designee shall be secured prior to each fundraiser activity. 
 
4
2. For athletics-based fund raising, the principal of the school receiving the primary 
benefit of the fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by the 
Superintendent, shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and 
any terms and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
 
3. The term “Approved Fundraising Entity” shall means an organization, group or 
boosters that satisfies the requirements of Community, Agency & Foundations 
(CAF) 219 and Community, Agency & Foundations (CAF) 215.  
 
4. All Approved Fundraising Entities shall submit an annual Memorandum of 
Understanding (MOU) setting forth all planned fund-raising activities for the 
ensuing school year. The MOU can be submitted up to two times per year. Should 
a group encounter an unexpected fundraising opportunity outside of the annual 
MOU schedule, they may submit one amendment for review and approval.   
 
5. The Superintendent shall have the authority to deny any fundraising activity 
he/she determines to be inappropriate or inconsistent with the shared community 
values and policies of the Manchester School District or from any group not in 
compliance with Board Policy CAF 215 and CAF 219.  
 
6. Any fundraiser collecting over $5,000 shall comply with the requirements of 
Fiscal 928: Gifts/ Donations, including any public hearing requirements. 
 
II. School & Student Based Fundraising:  
 
A. For the purpose of this policy, the term “School & Student Based Fundraising” shall 
mean fundraising that takes place in the schools and/or requires employee or student 
involvement. Examples of “School & Student Based Fundraising” include, but are not 
limited to, sale of restaurant cards, discount calendars, school-based scavenger hunts, 
school-based raffles, and other general fund-raising activities/solicitations that include 
student and/or school involvement.  
 
B. All School & Student Based Fundraising shall comply with the following:  
 
1. Student Participation 
 
 No student will be mandated to fundraise. 
 
 Students may not be penalized or sanctioned for choosing to not participate in 
fund-raising.   
 
 Students may not personally profit from fundraising activities. 
 
 Door-to-door sales are not recommended without parent supervision. 
 
5
 If students are going door to door a parent permission slip must be submitted 
before the start date of the fundraiser and kept on file at the school.  
 
2. Digital Platforms/Contracts 
 
 Prior to executing any agreements with online fundraising platforms, a 
thorough review of the vendor’s data privacy policy is required. 
 
 No coach, teacher, or other school employees may sign contracts with any 
vendor.  
 
 Any contract entered into without the express permission of the 
Superintendent is void. 
 
3. Incentives  
 
 No cash incentives may be paid to any student, employee, coach, advisor or 
family member in connection with fundraising activities.  
 
 Non-cash incentives may not exceed $50.00 in value in any calendar year. 
 
 Prize cards, cash grabs, cash payouts, commissions or similar incentives are 
prohibited.  
 
 Fundraising proceeds may not be used for end of the year gifts, cash or gift 
cards for students, employees or coaches. 
 
4. Payment and Accounting Practices  
 
 Must adhere to Manchester School District’s auditors’ current guidance  
 
5. Handling of Funds  
 
 All proceeds generated from such fundraising handled by students or 
employees of the district shall be deposited in compliance with Fiscal 924: 
Cash in School Buildings. Cash/Checks must be deposited within 24 hours of 
receipt whenever practicable. 
 
 Fundraising money handled by students or employees may not be stored in an 
unsecure area. 
 
 Access to fundraising money handled by students or employees should be 
limited to authorized individuals. 
 
 Students and employees involved in fundraising must properly document and 
keep accurate records for all fundraising activities. 
6
 To the extent that such fundraising activities involve the sale of any 
merchandise, restaurant/vendor discount cards*, books, or any other thing of 
material value, a record shall be kept, to include: 
 
a. Detailed plan of how the fundraiser will be run, what will be purchased, 
dates of the fundraising event(s), the company partnering for the 
fundraiser.  
 
b. The specific amount or number of items received by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising. 
 
c. Total amount or number of items sold and/or returned by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising. 
 
d. The amount of money collected by each person engaged in fundraising.  
 
e. Any merchandise or money that remains unaccounted for. 
 
f. No prize cards, cash grabs, etc. are permitted under any circumstances. 
Students may not profit individually from the sales of any fundraising 
items. No end of the year "gifts/ gift cards" can be given to students, 
employees/coaches with these funds.  
 
d.g. Employees overseeing fundraising and any Approved Fundraising 
Entities must meet with vendors to make sure they understand the 
requirements of this policy. 
 
6. Vendor Compensation  
 
 To the extent any individual, company, vendor or sponsor receive any of the 
proceeds (remuneration) from such fundraising activities, the terms and 
conditions for the receipt of such remuneration (and amount if known) shall 
be fully disclosed before approval by the Superintendent or designee.  
 
7. Final Accounting  
 
 At the conclusion of such fundraising activity, a full accounting shall be made 
to the Superintendent or the designee.  The accounting must include: 
 
a. Total amount of money raised. 
 
b. Any payments made to any individual or third party from the proceeds, 
 
7
b.c. Expenses. 
 
d. The net amount of the proceeds received by the Manchester School 
District or program, and  
 
e. Any unresolved discrepancies involving money or merchandise. 
 
f. The principal will maintain a file of all fundraisers and a separate copy 
will be maintained at the Superintendent’s office. 
 
 When funds are raised and the original purpose for the use of the funds is 
either exhausted or unavailable, such funds should revert to the student 
activities fund or other fund as designated by the Building Principal or 
designee.  
 
8. School & Student Fundraising Organized or Undertaken by an Approved 
Fundraising Entity 
 
 The Approved Fundraising Entity must comply with terms of the agreed-to 
MOU.  
 
 To the extent the fundraising involves students or employees of the District, 
the Approved Fundraising Entity must comply with all requirements for 
Student and School Based Fundraising except the proceeds from the 
fundraising activities may be retained by the Approved Fundraising Entity in 
whole, or in part, as set forth in the agreed-to MOU.  
 
 Money, merchandise, equipment, or other property donated/gifted to the 
Manchester School District and accepted by the District in accordance with 
Fiscal 928: Gifts/Donations shall become an asset of the Manchester School 
District upon acceptance.  Once accepted, donated funds or property shall be 
administered in accordance with applicable District policies.  
 
 Proceeds retained by the Approved Fundraising Entity shall be held and 
disbursed by its governing board in accordance with the organization’s bylaws 
and applicable state and federal laws.  
 
 If funds raised exceed the amount needed for the stated purpose, or the stated 
purpose has been fulfilled or no longer is available, the Approved Fundraising 
Entity will disburse the balance in accordance with its bylaws and applicable 
state and federal laws. 
 
III. Community Based Fundraising: No cash incentives shall be paid to any student or 
employee of the Manchester School District (including family members) in recognition 
of such fundraising activities. 
 
8
A. For the purpose of this policy, the term “Community Based Fundraising” shall mean 
fundraising that is undertaken by an Approved Fundraising Entity that takes place in 
the community and outside of the schools and generally does not require the 
involvement of students or employees of the district. Examples of “Community Based 
Fundraising” include, but are not limited to, banquets, golf tournaments, telethons, and 
other general fund-raising activities or solicitations that do not directly involve 
students or employees of the district.  
 
B. All Community Based Fundraising shall comply with the following:  
 
1. All community-based fundraising undertaken by an Approved Fundraising Entity 
shall be disclosed and included in the agreed-to annual MOU. 
 
2. All community-based fundraising undertaken by Approved Fundraising Entity 
shall comply with the terms of this policy. 
 
3. The proceeds from any community-based fundraising may be retained by the 
Approved Fundraising Entity in whole, or in part, as set forth in the agreed-to 
MOU.  
 
4. Community Based Fundraising shall be exempt from those rules set forth above 
that apply to the Handling of Funds, Payment and Accounting Practices, Vendor 
Compensation, and Final Accounting.  
 
5. Money, merchandise, equipment, or other property donated/gifted to the 
Manchester School District and accepted by the District in accordance with Fiscal 
928: Gifts/Donations shall become an asset of the Manchester School District 
upon acceptance.  Once accepted, donated funds or property shall be administered 
in accordance with applicable District policies.    
 
6. If funds raised exceed the amount needed for the stated purpose, or the stated 
purpose has been fulfilled or no longer is available, the Approved Fundraising 
Entity will disburse the balance in accordance with its bylaws and applicable state 
and federal laws. 
 
A.  
B. No student will be mandated to fundraise or sanctioned for non-participation in fund-
raising. 
C. No non-cash incentives with a value in excess of $50.00 shall be given to any 
employee or student of the Manchester School District (including family members) in 
recognition of such fundraising activities. 
D. All proceeds generated from such fundraising shall be deposited in compliance with 
Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings. 
E. To the extent that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any merchandise, 
restaurant/vendor discount cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a record

shall be kept as to the specific amount or number of items received by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising and total amount or number of items sold and/or returned 
by each individual engaged in such fundraising. 
F. No employee or student or organization associated with the Manchester School 
District shall be allowed to personally retain any item or proceeds secured or 
generated from such fundraising without the prior disclosure and approval of the 
Superintendent or his/her designee. 
G. To the extent any individual, company, vendor or sponsor receive any of the proceeds 
(remuneration) from such fundraising activities, the terms and conditions for the 
receipt of such remuneration (and amount if known) shall be fully disclosed before 
approval by the Superintendent or designee. 
H. At the conclusion of any fundraising activity, a full accounting shall be made to the 
Superintendent or the designee including the total amount of money raised, any 
payments made to any individual or third party from the proceeds, and the net amount 
of the proceeds received by the Manchester School District. 
I. For Athletics related funding raising, the Building Principal or his/her designee shall 
be responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms and conditions 
imposed by the Superintendent. 
J. For non-sports related fund raising, the principal of the school receiving the primary 
benefit of the fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by the 
Superintendent, shall responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any 
terms and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
K. The Superintendent shall have the authority to deny any fundraising activity he/she 
determines to be inappropriate or inconsistent with the shared community values of 
the Manchester School District. 
L. The Principal will maintain a file of all fundraisers and a separate copy will be 
maintained at the Superintendent’s office. 
M. Any contract entered into without the express permission of the Superintendent is 
void.  
 
For Athletics related fund raising, the Building Principal or his/ her designee shall be responsible 
for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms and conditions imposed by the 
Superintendent. For non-sports related group funding raising, the principal of the school 
receiving the primary benefit of the fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by 
the Superintendent, shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms 
and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
Fundraiser Cards/ Books:  To the extent that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any 
merchandise, restaurant/vendor discount cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a 
record shall be kept as to the specific amount or number of items received by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising and total amount or number of items sold and/or returned by each 
individual engaged in such fundraising. The following steps must be in place:  
 
1. A detailed plan of how the fundraiser will be run, what will be purchased, dates of 
the fundraising event(s), the company partnering for the fundraiser must be 
submitted to the Principal and the Superintendents or designee before any 
10
fundraisers can begin. The plan must include all the details from the fundraising 
partners.  
2. All money collected from any fundraiser must go to the program for the students. 
There can be no payoffs for participation from vendors to students and/or 
coaches/advisers.  
3. All money that is collected (cash and checks) must be secured as soon as possible 
and deposited within 24 hours of receipt. This secured location should have 
limited access to others.  
4. Each group or team must have a bookkeeping plan of how money collection will 
be tracked for each student. There must be a detailed system of how many cards 
or items are being sold by each student, how many were returned, and how many 
were unaccounted for.  
5. No prize cards, cash grabs, etc. are permitted under any circumstances. Students 
may not profit individually from the sales of any fundraising items. No end of the 
year "gifts/ gift cards" can be given to staff/coaches with these funds.  
6. Teams/groups must meet with the fundraising vendors to make sure they 
understand this.  
7. Clear guidance must be provided to students and families outlining that students 
must refrain from selling door-to-door. Students should be encouraged to sell to 
families and friends.  
8. The coach/adviser is responsible for the collection and bookkeeping of the funds 
relative to the fundraising of their program.  
9. No coach/adviser may sign contracts with any vendor. Such contracts should be 
processed through the Superintendent’s office or their designee.   
10. Any fundraiser collecting over $5,000 should comply with Fiscal 928: Gifts/ 
Donations for a public hearing.  
Athletic Boosters/Parent Teacher Groups (PTG)/ Parent Teacher Organizations (PTO)/ Parent 
Teacher Associations (PTA), booster clubs and other organizations fundraising with students of 
the Manchester School and on behalf of programs or schools in the Manchester NH School 
District will enter in a Memorandum of Understanding with the School District at the start of 
each school year to outline expectations and obligations This MOU will include any proposed 
crowd-funding campaigns expected throughout the year, and may be amended as necessary for 
an unanticipated campaigns started during the school year.

6. If funds raised exceed the amount needed for the stated purpose, or the stated 
purpose has been fulfilled or no longer is available, the Approved Fundraising 
Entity will disburse the balance in accordance with its bylaws and applicable state 
and federal laws.

536 FUND RAISING ACTIVITIES 
[JJE: Fund 
Raising Activities] 
The Board recognizes that students, parent/ teacher organizations, athletic groups, staff and 
others may wish to engage in fundraising activities to support the programs or offerings provided 
by the Manchester School District.  
Since the general public may see such fundraising efforts as carrying the endorsement of the 
Manchester School District, all such fundraising activities require the prior approval of the 
Superintendent and/or his/her designee.  
Fundraising activities governed explicitly by the policy include, but are not limited to, 
GoFundMe, Donors Choose or other similar web pages, cookie dough, candles, raffles, auctions, 
restaurant/vendor discount cards, book sales, sponsorships, walk or read-a-thons, or any other 
type of solicitation. This policy shall not apply to bake sales where the anticipated revenue will 
not exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00). Crowd-funding by employees on behalf of the 
District is governed by Fiscal 909.  
The Superintendent shall have the authority to impose conditions, limitations or restrictions on 
such fundraising activities in addition to the requirements of this policy as is deemed warranted 
or as dictated by accepted accounting standards and practices. Notwithstanding, the following 
conditions shall apply to all such fundraising activities:  
1. No cash incentives shall be paid to any student or employee of the Manchester School 
District (including family members) in recognition of such fundraising activities.
2. No student will be mandated to fundraise or sanctioned for non-participation in fund-
raising.
3. No non-cash incentives with a value in excess of $50.00 shall be given to any employee 
or student of the Manchester School District (including family members) in recognition of 
such fundraising activities.
4. All proceeds generated from such fundraising shall be deposited in compliance with 
Fiscal 924: Cash in School Buildings.
5. To the extent 
that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any merchandise, 
restaurant/vendor discount cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a record 
shall be kept as to the specific amount or number of items received by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising and total amount or number of items sold and/or returned by 
each individual engaged in such fundraising.
6. No employee or student or organization associated with the Manchester School District 
shall be allowed to personally retain any item or proceeds secured or generated from such 
fundraising without the prior disclosure and approval of the Superintendent or his/her 
designee.
21
7. To the extent any individual, company, vendor or sponsor receive any of the proceeds 
(remuneration) from such fundraising activities, the terms and conditions for the receipt 
of such remuneration (and amount if known) shall be fully disclosed before approval by 
the Superintendent or designee. 
8. At the conclusion of any fundraising activity, a full accounting shall be made to the 
Superintendent or the designee including the total amount of money raised, any payments 
made to any individual or third party from the proceeds, and the net amount of the 
proceeds received by the Manchester School District. 
9. For Athletics related funding raising, the Building Principal or his/her designee shall be 
responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms and conditions 
imposed by the Superintendent. 
10. For non-sports related funding raising, the principal of the school receiving the primary 
benefit of the fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by the 
Superintendent, shall responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms 
and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
11. The Superintendent shall have the authority to deny any fundraising activity he/she 
determines to be inappropriate or inconsistent with the shared community values of the 
Manchester School District. 
12. The Principal will maintain a file of all fundraisers and a separate copy will be 
maintained at the Superintendent’s office. 
13. Any contract entered into without the express permission of the Superintendent is void.  
 
For Athletics related fund raising, the Building Principal or his/ her designee shall be responsible 
for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms and conditions imposed by the 
Superintendent. For non-sports related group funding raising, the principal of the school 
receiving the primary benefit of the fundraising, or such other person as may be designated by 
the Superintendent, shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this policy and any terms 
and conditions imposed by the Superintendent. 
 
Fundraiser Cards/ Books:  To the extent that the fundraising activities involve the sale of any 
merchandise, restaurant/vendor discount cards, books, or any other thing of material value, a 
record shall be kept as to the specific amount or number of items received by each individual 
engaged in such fundraising and total amount or number of items sold and/or returned by each 
individual engaged in such fundraising. The following steps must be in place:  
 
1. A detailed plan of how the fundraiser will be run, what will be purchased, dates of 
the fundraising event(s), the company partnering for the fundraiser must be 
submitted to the Principal and the Superintendents or designee before any 
fundraisers can begin. The plan must include all the details from the fundraising 
partners.  
2. All money collected from any fundraiser must go to the program for the students. 
There can be no payoffs for participation from vendors to students and/or 
coaches/advisers.  
3. All money that is collected (cash and checks) must be secured as soon as possible 
and deposited within 24 hours of receipt. This secured location should have 
limited access to others.  
22
4. Each group or team must have a bookkeeping plan of how money collection will 
be tracked for each student. There must be a detailed system of how many cards 
or items are being sold by each student, how many were returned, and how many 
were unaccounted for.  
5. No prize cards, cash grabs, etc. are permitted under any circumstances. Students 
may not profit individually from the sales of any fundraising items. No end of the 
year "gifts/ gift cards" can be given to staff/coaches with these funds.  
6. Teams/groups must meet with the fundraising vendors to make sure they 
understand this.  
7. Clear guidance must be provided to students and families outlining that students 
must refrain from selling door-to-door. Students should be encouraged to sell to 
families and friends.  
8. The coach/adviser is responsible for the collection and bookkeeping of the funds 
relative to the fundraising of their program.  
9. No coach/adviser may sign contracts with any vendor. Such contracts should be 
processed through the Superintendent’s office or their designee.   
10. Any fundraiser collecting over $5,000 should comply with Fiscal 127: Gifts/ 
Donations for a public hearing.  
 
Athletic Boosters/Parent Teacher Groups (PTG)/ Parent Teacher Organizations (PTO)/ Parent 
Teacher Associations (PTA), booster clubs and other organizations fundraising with students of 
the Manchester School and on behalf of programs or schools in the Manchester NH School 
District will enter in a Memorandum of Understanding with the School District at the start of 
each school year to outline expectations and obligations This MOU will include any proposed 
crowd-funding campaigns expected throughout the year, and may be amended as necessary for 
an unanticipated campaigns started during the school year.  
 
All fundraising proceeds (purchases and/or physical items) that are obtained as part of any 
fundraising projects to benefit the Manchester School District will be an asset of the district.   
 
When funds are raised and the original purpose of the use of the funds is either exhausted or 
unavailable, such funds should revert to the student activities fund or other fund as designated by 
the Building Principal or designee.
